comment: Differences between firebase-testd and the official Local Emulator Suite that are intended and written down. A key is <scenarioId>#<stepId>. `documents` must name the text that publishes the divergence (a README section, a capability manifest entry, or a specification section); `reason` says what the difference is. Everything not listed here that differs is recorded as debt in DEBT.md, and `pnpm run check` gates a listed row against its recorded firebase-testd value, so a documented divergence still cannot drift silently.

firestore/missing-composite-index#admin-.reason: Under firestore.indexValidationPolicy = firebase, a query whose composite index is not in the index file is refused with FAILED_PRECONDITION and the fragment production would need. The official Firestore emulator serves the query as if the index existed; firebase-testd offers that as the `emulator` policy instead of as the default.
Same policy difference for an equality plus an inequality on another field.

firestore/missing-composite-index#client.reason: The same refusal reaches the gRPC client SDK: the target is removed with FAILED_PRECONDITION and the query resolves empty rather than failing the whole stream, so the client stays usable.

firestore/lite-rest-transport#query-need.reason: The same policy difference over the REST transport, where the SDK surfaces it as `failed-precondition`.

firestore/rest-error-shapes#runQuery-nee.reason: The REST envelope of the same refusal: HTTP 400 FAILED_PRECONDITION with the index fragment, where the official emulator answers 200 with results.

appcheck/exchange-and-jwks#exchange-a-re.reason: The official Local Emulator Suite serves no App Check exchange route at all, so the oracle answers 404. firebase-testd issues a locally signed token for a registered debug secret.

appcheck/exchange-and-jwks#exchange-an-u.reason: No route on the oracle (404) against the specified 403 PERMISSION_DENIED "App attestation failed." that firebase-testd returns for an unknown project, app, disabled app or secret alike.

appcheck/exchange-and-jwks#exchange-a-li.documents: capability manifest APPCHECK-REPLAY-1 (crates/firebase-testd/src/control.rs); docs/specifications/firebase-app-check.md sections 17 and 23
appcheck/exchange-and-jwks#exchange-a-li.reason: No route on the oracle (404). firebase-testd fails closed with 501 UNIMPLEMENTED / APP_CHECK_REPLAY_UNSUPPORTED rather than issuing a reusable token for a limited-use request.

appcheck/exchange-and-jwks#jwks.reason: The official suite serves no JWKS route (404). firebase-testd publishes this instance's single public App Check key as an RFC 7517 JWK Set.

appcheck/unenforced-header-matrix#firest.reason: The oracle issues no App Check token, so it cannot run the valid-token column at all; the row records the same request without the field and marks itself `noTokenIssuedBySide`.

appcheck/unenforced-header-matrix#auth-s.reason: The oracle issues no App Check token; see the Firestore row.

appcheck/unenforced-header-matrix#storag.reason: The oracle issues no App Check token; see the Firestore row.

appcheck/unenforced-header-matrix#callab.reason: The oracle issues no token, so its callable sees no app. firebase-testd forwards the verified token and the callable receives request.app with the registered app id, which is what section 13.4 requires of an unenforcing callable.

The official Functions emulator runs the runtime with token verification skipped, so any value in the field becomes an app with a null id. firebase-testd removes an unverifiable field before the runner can decode it, so the callable sees no app: strictly safer, and deliberately different.
Two App Check fields are ambiguous. The official emulator accepts the folded value as an app; firebase-testd classifies it as malformed and removes it.
The oracle issues no token, so its enforcing callable answers 401. firebase-testd presents a verified token and the callable runs with request.app populated.

With verification skipped, the official emulator admits an unverifiable token into an enforceAppCheck callable. firebase-testd refuses it with the callable 401 UNAUTHENTICATED envelope before the handler runs.
Duplicate App Check fields are admitted by the official emulator and refused by firebase-testd, for the same reason as the unenforcing row.

appcheck/unenforced-header-matrix#on-req.reason: The oracle issues no token, so it sends no field and its onRequest handler counts zero. Both sides pass the raw field list through unclassified, which is what the row is about.

appcheck/enforced-header-matrix#firestor.documents: capability manifest APPCHECK-ENFORCE-1 (crates/firebase-testd/src/control.rs); docs/specifications/firebase-app-check.md sections 12.1 and 17
appcheck/enforced-header-matrix#firestor.reason: The official emulators have no enforcement mode to configure, so they admit the request. This is the whole point of the variant: firebase-testd denies with 403 PERMISSION_DENIED before Security Rules and before any side effect.

appcheck/enforced-header-matrix#firestor.documents: capability manifest APPCHECK-ENFORCE-1 (crates/firebase-testd/src/control.rs); docs/specifications/firebase-app-check.md sections 12.1 and 17
appcheck/enforced-header-matrix#firestor.reason: Same: no enforcement on the oracle; 403 PERMISSION_DENIED on firebase-testd.
Same: no enforcement on the oracle; firebase-testd treats duplicate fields as malformed and denies.
Both sides admit, but the oracle admits because it never looked and cannot present a token; the row is marked `noTokenIssuedBySide` so the agreement is not read as parity.

appcheck/enforced-header-matrix#auth-sig.reason: No enforcement on the oracle; firebase-testd denies the end-user Identity Toolkit route with 403 and consumes no credential.
Same as the missing-field row, for an ambiguous duplicate field.
Both admit; the oracle only because it never looked. Marked `noTokenIssuedBySide`.

appcheck/enforced-header-matrix#storage-.reason: No enforcement on the oracle; firebase-testd denies the Firebase Storage dialect with the 403 Storage JSON error envelope.
Same as the missing-field row, for an ambiguous duplicate field.
Both admit; the oracle only because it never looked. Marked `noTokenIssuedBySide`.

appcheck/enforced-header-matrix#callable.reason: The oracle issues no token, so its enforcing callable answers 401; firebase-testd presents a verified token and the handler runs with request.app.
The official Functions emulator skips token verification and admits an unverifiable token; firebase-testd refuses it with the callable 401 envelope before the handler runs.
Duplicate fields are admitted by the official emulator and refused by firebase-testd.

functions/callable-auth-context#a-forged.documents: capability manifest APPCHECK-FUNCTIONS-1, "callable Authorization integrity" (crates/firebase-testd/src/control.rs); docs/specifications/firebase-app-check.md section 25 decision 3
functions/callable-auth-context#a-forged.reason: The official Functions emulator runs the runtime with token verification skipped, so any Bearer value produces a context with hasAuth true and a null uid. firebase-testd verifies the ID token against the target project's registry and reinserts only a resolved user, so a forged value produces no Auth context at all.

functions/callable-auth-context#bearer-o.documents: capability manifest APPCHECK-FUNCTIONS-1, "callable Authorization integrity" (crates/firebase-testd/src/control.rs); docs/specifications/firebase-app-check.md section 25 decision 3
functions/callable-auth-context#bearer-o.reason: `Bearer owner` is the privileged emulator credential. The official emulator hands it to the callable as an authenticated context with a null uid; firebase-testd never treats it as a callable user identity.
